root_idea.summary: The root chiefly conveys turning or directing oneself toward something; a separate branch concerns roundness and encircling coverings.
root_idea.development: The directional branch extends to asking, contentment with what one has, sufficiency, and several acts of extending or inclining toward an object. A divergent elevation sense is explicitly attested in the Quranic expression مُقْنِعِي رُؤُوسِهِمْ, while the roundness branch yields sand formations, trays, and head coverings.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-only plural inflection is normalized to the singular active-participle citation form مُقْنِعٌ.
The Quranic inflected form is presented under the singular active-participle citation form قَانِعٌ.

senses.definition: One who raises or holds the head aloft.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction مُقْنِعِي رُؤُوسِهِمْ, it describes heads raised upward rather than inclined downward.

senses.definition: A petitioner or beggar who asks without persistent insistence.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic distribution of sacrificial meat, the term is lexically explained as one who asks and is satisfied with what is given without pressing the request.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Contentment; making do with a small amount of needed worldly provisions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related verb قَنِعَ denotes being satisfied or content, as distinct from قَنَعَ in the asking sense.
This is the verbal asking sense corresponding to the petitioner noun قَانِعٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be content or satisfied with a thing.
To put on a helmet or other head armor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is explained by analogy with a woman putting on a head covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A satisfactory or acceptable authority, especially one whose judgment or evidence is sufficient to rely upon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is reported as usable for masculine and feminine, singular, dual, and plural referents.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sufficiency; something adequate to satisfy or suffice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions stating that a matter provides enough or is satisfactory.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman’s head covering worn over the khimār and wider than it.
The integument of the heart, or pericardium.
To cover the head with blows from a sword or whip.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression is figurative, as though the blows formed a covering over the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Directing or extending toward something, including turning the face toward it or extending the hand in supplication.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same directional construction is also applied to extending an animal’s head toward water and to inclining a vessel so that its water runs downward.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For camels or sheep to incline toward a pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction with لِـ marking the pasture toward which they turn.
This belongs to the root’s separate roundness branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tray-like platter on which a gift is presented.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal usage associated with a rounded or encircling form.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Contentment with a thing is represented as a Classical meaning.
Acceptability in judgment or evidence is represented.
The woman’s head covering is represented.
The anatomical heart covering is represented.
The Quran-attested asking or begging sense is represented.
Pointer-only cross-reference; the unit supplies no lexical definition.

cautions: The supplied contextual rendering for قَانِعٌ is “the needy who do not ask,” whereas the direct lexical evidence supports “one who asks or begs,” particularly without insistence; this is a genuine interpretive variation.
The Lane citation recorded as “Kur, xxii. 37” is not converted into a modern verse location. The Quran example here uses the independently supplied QAC occurrence at 22:36.
